attacks.claim: The plan replaces the open, self-hostable sync server with a proprietary, hosted-only dependency, contradicting the README/charter promise that users can self-host sync and own their data. The stride-server image is archived in 5.0, leaving ~3,000 self-hosted instances with no supported path.
attacks.evidence: "the server component is available only as the hosted Cirrus Cloud service" ... "Cirrus Cloud becomes the single sync backend and the stride-server Docker image is archived."

attacks.claim: Single-provider lock-in with high exit cost: the on-device store, sync protocol, and server are all Cirrus-owned under a commercial license, and the free tier is a 100k-device cap with 90k current users, leaving ~10% headroom and no stated pricing after the free tier.
attacks.evidence: "free up to 100k monthly active devices; our 90k fits the free tier" ... "Cirrus Cloud becomes the single sync backend"

attacks.claim: Open-source (MIT) project distributing a proprietary commercial-license binary SDK, and the plan silently changes the licensing/redistribution posture and the stated charter without an evidenced license review or charter amendment.
attacks.evidence: "distributed as a prebuilt binary ... under the Cirrus commercial license" ... ABSENT: license compatibility review against MIT and charter update

attacks.claim: Workout data including GPS tracks is now replicated to a third-party cloud by default, a material change in data custody for users who previously self-hosted; no consent, data-processing terms, or residency statement is given.
attacks.evidence: "Cirrus replicates to Cirrus Cloud when connectivity returns" ... ABSENT: consent flow, data processing agreement, data residency

attacks.claim: Account deletion depends on a third-party admin API with a 30-day window, but there is no verification that Cirrus-held replicas, backups, or tombstones (retained 90 days) are purged, so deletion guarantees are unverified.
attacks.evidence: "removes the Cirrus user record and all synced records via the Cirrus admin API within 30 days" ... ABSENT: verification of backups/replicas deletion

attacks.claim: Removing legacy REST sync and archiving the server image in 5.0 is a one-way door for self-hosters; the plan has no rollback path to self-hosted sync if Cirrus pricing, availability, or the SDK changes.
attacks.evidence: "Legacy REST sync is removed in app 5.0" ... "the stride-server Docker image is archived"

attacks.claim: The central claim that Cirrus fixes partial uploads and duplicates is unprototyped; the Week 1 spike is the only validation, yet the plan commits 5 weeks, 3 contributors, and a beta to 500 users before the spike result is known. The 'never leaves a partial workout' guarantee is asserted without evidence.
attacks.evidence: "Week 1: Cirrus integration spike" ... "a dropped connection never leaves a partial workout"

attacks.claim: The 23% figure and the 80% success metric lack a stated baseline or source.
attacks.evidence: "23% of sync-related GitHub issues in the last 6 months" ... "down 80% within 2 months of 4.0"

attacks.claim: Halt criterion is inadequate: crash-free sessions is the only rollback signal, but sync data-loss/duplication is the target failure and is not monitored; a regression in sync correctness would not halt the rollout.
attacks.evidence: "halting if crash-free sessions drop below 99.3%" ... ABSENT: sync data-loss/duplicate monitoring

attacks.claim: Migration failure modes are underspecified: the backup copy is made before migration, but the 3.x restore path and 30-day/two-sync deletion rule can leave a duplicate or stale store, and there is no defined behavior when Cirrus sync is unreachable during migration.
attacks.evidence: "the backup is deleted only after 30 days and two successful syncs" ... ABSENT: behavior when Cirrus unreachable

attacks.claim: Conflict model is internally inconsistent: append-only after finish with per-field LWW for edits, plus 90-day tombstones, means an offline device offline >90 days can resurrect a deleted workout, contradicting the stated resurrection guarantee.
attacks.evidence: "Deletes are tombstones retained 90 days so an offline device cannot resurrect a deleted workout"

attacks.claim: HLC is stamped on device, so clock skew and client-set timestamps can let a malicious or misconfigured device win LWW; no bound or validation is specified.
attacks.evidence: "per-field last-writer-wins using a hybrid logical clock stamped on device"

attacks.claim: Tombstone and per-record change tracking growth is unbounded by design for 90k+ users; no size or compaction estimate is given, and the 10x-100x load case (up to ~9M devices) exceeds the free tier cap by far.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: load and storage estimate; "up to 100k monthly active devices"

attacks.claim: No cost model: the free tier covers only 90k of the stated base with 10k headroom, and growth beyond 100k or post-free-tier pricing is unquantified, creating an unbounded recurring spend that the plan does not budget.
attacks.evidence: "free up to 100k monthly active devices; our 90k fits the free tier" ... ABSENT: post-tier pricing and budget

attacks.claim: Migration and sync-state feedback to users (e.g., failed migration, pending sync) is not described, so screen-reader and visually impaired users have no specified accessible status signal.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: user-facing status/error UX for migration and sync

attacks.claim: The plan does not address the self-hosting user base's needs; it solves the offline problem by removing their option rather than offering an alternative.
attacks.evidence: "Self-hosted servers keep working through the transition" ... "Cirrus Cloud becomes the single sync backend"

attacks.claim: Contributor dispatch: 3 contributors on a 5-week build with a proprietary third-party SDK whose lifecycle and support terms are not established.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: SDK support SLA and ownership of the Cirrus dependency
